name: Sidetic
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Wikipedia, "Sidetic language" (accessed 2026-09-17), used only for its bibliography
sources.note: No phonology beyond 'aphaeresis is frequent in names in Sidetic... as is syncope'; no stress statement. Supplied the bibliography (Pérez Orozco, Zinko & Zinko 2019, Merlin & Pisaniello 2025, Kassian 2013, Nollé, Neumann, Rizza 2005, Kadmos 2025 papers).

sources.citation: Kloekhorst, Alwin. 2022. "Anatolian." In Thomas Olander (ed.), The Indo-European Language Family: A Phylogenetic Perspective, 63-82. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (Open Access). doi:10.1017/9781108758666.005
sources.note: Nothing on Sidetic stress. Sidetic is described on p. 65 ('attested in some ten inscriptions on coins and stone... The number of textual remains is very low, so we only know a few facts about Sidetic grammar and lexicon') and its subgrouping is discussed pp. 70-71; the only accent mention is a Proto-Anatolian sound law (PIE accented *ó lengthened, p. 67).

sources.citation: Woudhuizen, Fred C. 2020. "On the Reading and Interpretation of the Two Longer Sidetic Inscriptions S I.2.1 and S I.2.5." Živa Antika 70(1-2): 17-34. doi:10.47054/ZIVA20701-2017w
sources.note: Silent: discusses sign values (vowel /a/, sibilants, punctuation strokes) and readings of two inscriptions; grep for accent/stress/prosody gives zero hits in the 18-page text.

sources.citation: Pandey, Anshuman. 2019. "Introducing the Sidetic Script." Unicode document L2/19-106, 2 pp.
sources.note: Script-encoding note only; nothing on the language's phonology or stress.

sources.citation: eDiAna (Digital Philological-Etymological Dictionary of the Minor Ancient Anatolian Corpus Languages), LMU Munich, corpus page
sources.note: Corpus page confirms a Sidetic corpus (2021) numbered after Nollé 2001: 625-646 and cites Zinko & Zinko 2019; no language description or stress statement visible.

sources.citation: Merlin, Stella & Valerio Pisaniello. 2025. "Late Languages of Marginal Attestation: Pamphylian, Sidetic, and Pisidian." In Contacts of Languages and Peoples in the Hittite and Post-Hittite World, 360-380. Leiden: Brill.

sources.note: Most recent synthesis of Sidetic grammar/phonology; open-access license (CC BY-NC-ND) per Crossref, so a browser download should work even though brill.com blocks our machine; the one place a modern statement on (un)knowability of Sidetic accent would appear.

sources.citation: Zinko, Christian & Michaela Zinko. 2019. "Sidetisch – Ein Update zu Schrift und Sprache." In R. I. Kim, J. Mynářová & P. Pavúk (eds.), Hrozný and Hittite: The First Hundred Years, 416-432. Leiden: Brill.
